record.context_brief: Potential dependence and sigma = d/2 threshold
record.original_question: For eigenvalue sums of the form sum_j |E_j|^{-sigma} delta(E_j)^{gamma + sigma} associated with semiclassical Schrödinger operators with complex-valued potentials, how does the hbar-growth exponent depend on the choice of potential V, and what role does the threshold sigma = d/2 play in determining whether an hbar^{-d} bound is valid or violated?

evidence.quote: Similarly, to which extent does the power of ℏ depend on the choice of the potential? Also, it would be interesting to understand the role of the purported threshold σ = d/ 2 for the validity/violation of an ℏ^{-d}-bound on ∑_j |Ej|^{-σ} δ(Ej)^{γ + σ}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and consider the semiclassical Schrödinger operator
$$H_\hbar = -\hbar^2\Delta + V$$
on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, where $\hbar\in(0,1]$ and $V:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{C}$ is a (suitably decaying) complex-valued potential. Let $\{E_j\}_{j}$ denote the discrete eigenvalues of $H_\hbar$ in $\mathbb{C}\setminus[0,\infty)$, counted with algebraic multiplicity, and define
$$\delta(E_j) := \operatorname{dist}(E_j,[0,\infty)),$$
the distance from $E_j$ to the essential spectrum of $-\hbar^2\Delta$. For parameters $\sigma\ge 0$ and $\gamma\ge 0$, consider the eigenvalue sums
$$S_{\sigma,\gamma}(V,\hbar) \;=\; \sum_{j} |E_j|^{-\sigma}\,\delta(E_j)^{\gamma+\sigma}.$$

Investigate the following two questions:

(1) How does the optimal exponent $\alpha = \alpha(V,\sigma,\gamma,d)$ in any semiclassical bound of the form
$$S_{\sigma,\gamma}(V,\hbar) \;\le\; C(V,\sigma,\gamma,d)\,\hbar^{-\alpha}\qquad(\hbar\to 0^+)$$
depend on the choice of the complex potential $V$? In particular, identify classes of potentials for which $\alpha$ differs from the Weyl exponent $d$.

(2) Determine the precise role of the threshold $\sigma = d/2$: prove or disprove that the Weyl-type bound
$$S_{\sigma,\gamma}(V,\hbar) \;\le\; C(V,\sigma,\gamma,d)\,\hbar^{-d}$$
holds for all admissible complex $V$ when $\sigma < d/2$ (respectively $\sigma > d/2$), and exhibit explicit complex potentials that violate this $\hbar^{-d}$ bound on the other side of the threshold.
artifact.category_tag: Semiclassical Schrödinger operators with complex potentials
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of three explicitly stated open problems concerning Schrödinger operators with complex potentials that appear to violate Weyl-type semiclassical asymptotics. No subsequent work resolving the potential-dependence of the $\hbar$-exponent or the precise role of the $\sigma=d/2$ threshold for the $\hbar^{-d}$ bound on $\sum_j|E_j|^{-\sigma}\delta(E_j)^{\gamma+\sigma}$ was located.

status_evidence.title: Schrödinger operators with complex potentials (arXiv:2409.11285)
status_evidence.snippet: We explain in which sense Schrödinger operators with complex potentials appear to violate locality (or Weyl's asymptotics), and we pose three open problems related to this phenomenon.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an explicitly open problem about complex-potential Schrödinger operators and a possible $\sigma=d/2$ threshold for $\hbar^{-d}$ bounds.
